On Tuesday, March 19, 2013 9:03:32 AM UTC-4, David Blei wrote:
fellow stanimals,

thanks for setting up functions to compute the log joint and its gradient in R.

i'd like to compute these items without running any iterations of HMC.
 i tried setting iter = 0, but to no avail.

my question: how can i get a stan object without running any
iterations, in order to evaluate log joints and gradients?

I think what you did works despite the error message that resurrected itself for v1.2.0

ecode <-
"
parameters {
  real<lower=0> y[2];
}
model {
  y ~ exponential(1);
}
"
fit <- stan(model_code = ecode, iter = 0)

yields

TRANSLATING MODEL 'ecode' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'ecode' NOW.
Error in config_argss(chains = chains, iter = iter, warmup = warmup, thin = thin,  :
  parameter 'iter' should be a positive integer
error specification of arguments; sampling not done

but the object is actually created just fine and you can call log_prob on it

fit
Stan model 'ecode' does not contain samples.
log_prob(fit, c(1,2))
[1] -7.107338

To avoid the disturbing error message, you can call stan() with chains = 0

fit <- stan(model_code = ecode, chains = 0)

TRANSLATING MODEL 'ecode' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'ecode' NOW.
the number of chains is less than 1; sampling not done

Ben

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: computing log joints
parts:
log_prob is defined as a method (in terms of the concept of OOP), so help(log_prob) will show the whole doc about stanfit, where you can find the doc about log_prob.  Now I think it might be better to single out the doc.

Unfortunately, the current implementation is doing double computation (more computation for gradients).  I was suggesting get the lp__ the same time as the gradients, https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-dev/Mus4GiHefTY/_tUqXNPyekUJ

So when the underlying API gives us both lp__ and the gradient, we can save some computation. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: computing log joints
parts:
On 3/21/13 10:38 AM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> log_prob is defined as a method (in terms of the concept of OOP), so help(log_prob) will show the whole doc about
> stanfit, where you can find the doc about log_prob. Now I think it might be better to single out the doc.
>
> Unfortunately, the current implementation is doing double computation (more computation for gradients). I was
> suggesting get the lp__ the same time as the gradients, https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-dev/Mus4GiHefTY/_tUqXNPyekUJ
>
> So when the underlying API gives us both lp__ and the gradient, we can save some computation.

If by the underlying API, you mean the model API,
it already gives you both at the same time. Here's
the spec of the relevant function in the abstract
base class model::prob_grad defined in src/model/prob_grad.hpp
(line 91):

virtual double grad_log_prob(std::vector<double>& params_r,
std::vector<int>& params_i,
std::vector<double>& gradient,
std::ostream* output_stream = 0) = 0;

You pass in a gradient to vector to fill and the function
returns the log probability.

We definitely need some more basic API doc for doxygen for this.
We'll try to tackle the doc issue along with the refactoring.

- Bob
